cycle.coreQuestion: What does the IgboKal cosmological teaching of Ọ́nwá Okike — Distribution — reveal about the architecture of community life, and how does the celebration of Sharing transform how we build, inhabit, and sustain communities in IgboKal 5004?
cycle.title: The Sacred Distribution

days.bodyFocus: “Sharing begins when the person who needs something can say what would help.”
days.echo: Ask someone what would make their day easier. Listen without correcting them or promising more than you can give.
days.prompt: Whose voice is missing when your household or community decides what to share?

days.bodyFocus: “A skill makes a different kind of light when someone else can use it.”
days.echo: Offer to teach one small skill, from saving seeds to finding forms. Let learners practice in their own way.
days.prompt: What could someone in your circle do for themselves if you showed them how?

days.bodyFocus: “A gift may arrive in minutes, carried by relationships tended for years.”
days.echo: Trace recent help to someone whose work went unnoticed. Thank them privately and ask what would make their work easier.
days.prompt: What quiet act of care keeps something moving in your community?

days.bodyFocus: “What the earth yields becomes sustenance only when it reaches a table.”
days.echo: Choose a usable item or food you can spare. Confirm it’s wanted, then arrange a handoff that suits you both.
days.prompt: Where does something useful go unused while someone nearby could make use of it?

days.bodyFocus: “If we can only ask for what is offered, we may never say what we want.”
days.echo: Choose a usable item or food you can spare. Confirm it’s wanted, then arrange a handoff that suits you both.
days.prompt: What does your community want to make possible together that its usual offers do not address?

days.bodyFocus: “An inherited practice stays alive when the next hands can make it their own.”
days.echo: Recall a practice & name your teacher. With permission when needed, demonstrate one step and invite someone to adapt it.
days.prompt: Which way of sharing did an elder or forebear pass down that could serve someone today?

days.bodyFocus: “The yam grows out of sight; a new way of sharing may need the same patience.”
days.echo: Ask to help someone building a quiet initiative. Offer one manageable thing: a ride, a tool, a spare hour.
days.prompt: What small effort in your community needs support before it is ready to be seen?

days.bodyFocus: “A shared tool changes what people can make for themselves.”
days.echo: Choose one tool, space, or task. Ask a willing person to use it on their own terms.
days.prompt: What do people rely on you to provide that they could help shape or manage instead?

days.bodyFocus: “A promise begins to travel when it has a person, a place, and a time.”
days.echo: Agree on one act of sharing with a willing person. Put the time and your part in the calendar today.
days.prompt: Which intention to share has remained an intention because nobody has set a time?

days.bodyFocus: “Cut the rule that keeps people out, not the care that holds people together.”
days.echo: Write down the Rule. Ask someone affected by it what it costs them, and propose one change together.
days.prompt: PORTAL DAY: What Rule can I change to Open the Way for inclusion and sharing?

days.bodyFocus: What leaves your hands is only half the story; what reaches another is the rest.”
days.echo: Ask one recipient privately whether the help arrived in a usable form. Let the answer, guide the next offer.
days.prompt: What would tell you that a recent offer actually met the need it was meant to meet?

days.bodyFocus: “A room is not truly shared if only one person can decide when it opens.”
days.echo: Invite those affected to shape one decision about hours, turns, or eligibility. Clarify decisions and action processes.
days.prompt: Who uses a resource you help manage but has little say in how it is shared?

days.bodyFocus: “Care makes room for an answer it did not expect.”
days.echo: Make one offer that includes a choice and an easy way to decline. If the person says no, accept it.
days.prompt: When have you offered what was easiest to give rather than what someone wanted to receive?

days.bodyFocus: “When thanks names the work, the people who do it are harder to forget.”
days.echo: Thank someone for a specific act and its impact. Ask before public recognition, and offer to share in the work.
days.prompt: Whose particular contribution gets lost when everyone is thanked in the same breath?

days.bodyFocus: “A gift can be received without turning it into a debt.”
days.echo: Accept welcome help today with a simple thank-you. Otherwise, write down one kind of help you could comfortably ask for.
days.prompt: What makes it hard for you to accept care when you cannot return it right away?

days.bodyFocus: “The unborn cannot ask us to save their portion.”
days.echo: Set aside one seed, story, skill, or resource for a future learner or steward. Record its source & continued relevance.
days.prompt: What have you received from those before you that you would like someone after you to inherit?

days.bodyFocus: A word for sharing carries farther when it names something people recognize.”
days.echo: Recall the phrase or gesture and write down one occasion when someone used it. Keep its wording for shared memory.
days.prompt: What family phrase, home-language word, or remembered gesture tells you that sharing has taken place?

days.bodyFocus: “A smooth account of sharing can hide the roughest part of getting there.”
days.echo: Describe one barrier without identity disclosure. Bring it to a person or group that can help change it.
days.prompt: What difficulty with access is familiar to those who face it but rarely named where decisions are made?

days.bodyFocus: “Like a first yam brought to the table, an insight can be offered before all the work is done.”
days.echo: Share one specific lesson with someone it concerns. Ask for one correction before you repeat it elsewhere.
days.prompt: Which lesson from this month is ready to be tested with others?

days.bodyFocus: “An invitation reaches its destination only when people know how to answer it.”
days.echo: Rewrite one notice in everyday language and ask an intended reader to test it.
days.prompt: Which notice about shared help assumes knowledge, time, or technology that not everyone has?

days.bodyFocus: “From above, the place where a gift stalls is as important as the place where it begins.”
days.echo: Sketch one route from source to use. Mark one point where it stalls; ask people what would help it move.
days.prompt: Where along the route from making to receiving does a shared resource most often stop?

days.bodyFocus: “A brighter future begins where someone can see a way through that was not there before.”
days.echo: Describe an experience in three steps. Choose one step you can test  with the people who would use it.
days.prompt: What would young people be able to find, borrow, or learn in a year if you changed one route of access now?

days.bodyFocus: “The past may reveal a way of sharing that habit has taught us to overlook.”
days.echo: Write an observation grounded in one story you know about that elder. Mark it as your reflection, not their words.
days.prompt: What might a remembered elder notice about the way your community shares now?

days.bodyFocus: “A share is not equal when one person must travel much farther to claim it.”
days.echo: Compare two routes to the same resource. Test the harder route and learn the Share Lesson.
days.prompt: Who pays the most in time, travel, or effort to use something your community calls shared?

days.bodyFocus: “Carry forward the gift that found its way, and remember how it got there.”
days.echo: Review your notes. Record what moved, what made it possible, and one lesson you can pass on.
days.prompt: Which act this month shows that something reached a person or place that needed it?

days.bodyFocus: “The work lasts when more than one person knows how to tend it.”
days.echo: Invite a willing partner to shape a sustainable version of one practice. Agree on what each of you can do.
days.prompt: Which practice deserves to continue without depending on one person’s constant effort?

days.bodyFocus: “The month can close while the care it set in motion continues.”
days.echo: Note: what we received, what we passed on, and what still needs to reach someone. Meet one need next month.
days.prompt: Which relationship or quiet practice will keep this month’s learning alive after the last Kapsule?

days.bodyFocus: “What took form in Ọ́nwá Ànà and found its place in Ọ́nwá Òkìkè now meets the test of exchange.”
days.echo: Name one new condition that would make an exchange fair. Carry that condition carefully into the new month.
days.prompt: What will you carry into Ọ́nwá Ajaana so that what you receive and what you offer both sustain life?

izuThemes.focus: The month opens at the root — the ground level of existence. Before celebrate sharing can be expressed in community life, it must be felt in the body, sensed in the earth, trusted as a foundation rather than a concept. Today: simply arrive.
izuThemes.subtitle: Entering Ọ́nwá Okike

izuThemes.focus: The sacral principle of creative desire asks: what does your community want from distribution? Not what it needs, not what it is supposed to want — what does it genuinely desire?
izuThemes.subtitle: The Desire for Distribution

izuThemes.focus: The solar plexus — Mpio Oku — is the center of will. In Month 10, will is required: the discipline to actually practice celebrate sharing rather than merely intend it. What does this month's celebration require of your will?
izuThemes.subtitle: The Will to Celebrate Sharing

izuThemes.focus: At the midpoint, the Heart center of Ire Oku asks: can you love distribution? Not the idea — the reality? With all its complexity, its difficulty, its demand?
izuThemes.subtitle: The Heart of Distribution

izuThemes.focus: Odu Oku — the throat that encodes. What is the name of distribution in your community? Not the generic term — the specific, living name that your community uses when it is most itself?
izuThemes.subtitle: Naming Distribution in Your Community

izuThemes.focus: From the elevated platform of Ogwe Oku, distribution appears in its full cosmological context — as a stage in the life-process that was inevitable, necessary, and perfectly timed. Can your community engage impactfully with this theme?
izuThemes.subtitle: The Elevated View of Distribution

izuThemes.focus: Uje Oku — the crown, the summit. To seal this month at the crown is to consecrate its learning at the highest register of consciousness. What is the crown teaching of distribution for your community?
izuThemes.subtitle: The Crown of Distribution
